blogs.content: With the rising adoption of electric vehicles, more customers are actively seeking sustainable commuting options. This shift has fueled a growing demand for budget-friendly yet smart choices in electric mobility. Among them, many are on the lookout for electric two-wheeler scooters priced under ₹1 lakh that deliver the best riding experience without compromising on quality or style.Today, we bring you a list of the top four electric scooters in India under ₹1 lakh.Ampere Magnus Neo   Debuted at Auto Expo 2025 in Delhi, this latest offering from Greaves Electric Mobility has made a significant impact on India's affordable and stylish electric scooter segment. As an upgraded version of the widely popular Magnus EX, this electric scooter boasts a certified range of over 100 kilometers, a top speed of 65 kmph, and a robust LFP battery with a five-year warranty. Priced at ₹79,999 (ex-showroom), the Magnus Neo is designed to make eco-friendly commuting more accessible with enhanced features. It is powered by a Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) battery, offering a warranty of five years or 75,000 kilometers, whichever comes first. Before its debut at Auto Expo 2025, the Magnus Neo underwent a rigorous 2,300+kilometer test ride from Bengaluru to Delhi, demonstrating its durability and efficiency. The scooter is available in five eye-catching colors—Metallic Red, Glacial White, Ocean Blue, Galactic Grey, and Glossy Black—and comes with optional smart connectivity, USB charging, and a reverse mode for added convenienceLink: https://evindia.online/news/greaves-electric-mobilitys-ampere-two-wheelers-achieve-53-yoy-growth-in-januaryhttps://evindia.online/product/ampere-ev-neo Bajaj Chetak 2903 Series Bajaj’s 2903 series Chetak electric scooter is making waves in the E2W market with its striking design, impressive performance, and affordability. Available for purchase in India at a starting price of approximately ₹96,000 (ex-showroom), the scooter offers a claimed range of 123 km on a single charge. Designed for a smooth riding experience, the Chetak 2903 features a sturdy metal body that effectively absorbs shocks from bumps and obstacles on the road. It also comes equipped with a vibrant, high-resolution digital display that provides clear and detailed ride data. For braking, the scooter is fitted with a disc brake at the front and a drum brake at the rear, complemented by a Combined Braking System (CBS) for enhanced safety. Powered by a 2.88 kWh battery, it achieves a top speed of approximately 63 km/h. The Chetak 2903 is available in five stylish color options—Brooklyn Black, Cyber White, Racing Red, Azure Blue, and Lime Yellow. https://evindia.online/electric-vehicle-companies/bajaj-evhttps://evindia.online/news/bajaj-introduces-all-new-chetak-3501-and-3502-electric-scooter-all-you-need-to-knowTVS iQube 2.2 kWh The TVS iQube 2.2 kWh is a strong contender in the electric two-wheeler market, making it a preferred choice for E2W enthusiasts. The scooter is available in two elegant color options—Pearl White and Walnut Brown. Equipped with a dual braking system, it features a disc brake at the front and a drum brake at the rear for enhanced safety. Key highlights of the iQube include a digital speedometer and odometer, Bluetooth-enabled mobile connectivity, a tail light, navigation support, and more. The scooter takes approximately 3 hours to charge up to 80-90% and offers a range of 75 km on a single charge. Powered by a 3 kW motor, it delivers a smooth and efficient riding experience. While the price may vary slightly across different regions in India, the estimated cost falls between ₹95,000 and ₹1,05,000, depending on available offers and discounts. https://youtu.be/F_wJVFgWp3w?feature=shared Ola S1X 3 kWh The Ola S1 X 3kWh variant is an excellent choice for customers seeking an affordable and smart mobility solution. Packed with advanced features, it enhances the overall riding experience with a 10.9 cm (4.3-inch) segmented display, providing riders with essential information at a glance. Additionally, the scooter offers smart connectivity, enabling users to control various ride aspects through the Ola Electric App. It is available in five attractive colors: Industrial Silver, Jet Black, Midnight Blue, Passion Red, and Porcelain White. With a battery capacity of 3 kWh, the S1 X 3kWh offers a range of approximately 75 km on a single charge. It is powered by an IPM motor paired with a 3 kWh battery pack, delivering a certified range of 115 km and a top speed that ensures a smooth and efficient ride in urban settings. The introductory price starts at around ₹86,000, making it a competitive option in the electric scooter segment. Ola also offers a battery warranty of 8 years or 80,000 km, whichever comes first, with an option to extend it to 1,00,000 km.1,25,000 km for ₹5,999 + GST and ₹12,999 + GST, respectively, if you ride a lot more than that. https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?id=666874395778593https://evindia.online/product/ola-electric-s1-x-ev-3kwh

blogs.title: Comprehensive Review 2025: Smart Features in Jio's Revolutionary Electric Bicycle
blogs.subtitle: In an era where smart technology intersects with sustainable mobility, Jio is set to revolutionize India's transportation landscape with their inno...
blogs.author: Akshesh
blogs.description: In an era where smart technology intersects with sustainable mobility, Jio is set to revolutionize India's transportation landscape with their innovative electric bicycle.
blogs.content: This groundbreaking venture promises to merge affordable eco-conscious travel with cutting-edge connectivity, targeting a market segment often overlooked by premium e-bike manufacturers.As India grapples with urban congestion and environmental concerns, Jio's 2025 entry into the electric bicycle market represents more than just another product launch. It signals a paradigm shift in how technology can democratize sustainable transportation, offering features previously reserved for high-end electric vehicles at a price point accessible to students and daily commuters.Electric Bicycle Innovation from JioJio Electric Cycle plans to bring affordable electric bicycles to Indian roads in 2025. Building on their existing Leeji bicycle brand, the new e-bikes will feature an impressive range of up to 80 kilometers per charge. The company targets students, daily commuters, and lower-income groups with this eco-conscious transportation option.Smart Display and User Interface FeaturesThe bicycle comes equipped with a weather-resistant display that shows speed, battery status, and navigation details. Riders can control the interface through a handlebar-mounted joystick, while the screen automatically adjusts brightness based on surrounding light conditions. The Best Smart Displays remains readable in direct sunlight, making it practical for everyday use.GPS Navigation and Route TrackingThe bicycle features built-in GPS tracking that provides centimeter-level location accuracy. Riders receive turn-by-turn directions through the intelligent routing app and real-time traffic updates during their journeys. The system allows users to share their routes with others, making group rides and commute coordination simple. This integration of precise navigation supports safer, more efficient cycling experiences.Smartphone Connectivity and Companion AppThe e-bicycle supports 5G connectivity, offering an integrated mobile experience. The Home Assistant lets riders monitor battery status, locate charging stations, and track ride statistics. Users can join local cycling communities through the app and receive real-time notifications about their bicycle's status. The system requires consistent network coverage for complete functionality.Battery Management System and Range EstimationThe battery system combines advanced cell chemistry with thermal monitoring to provide up to 100 kilometers of range. The system includes overcharge protection and short-circuit prevention features, while actively monitoring temperature levels during operation. The battery state estimation power management system adjusts output based on riding conditions, providing riders with accurate range estimates through the display interface.Regenerative Braking TechnologyThe e-bicycle features a kinetic energy recovery system that converts braking force into stored electrical power. The system offers multiple recovery modes, allowing riders to select their preferred balance between energy capture and braking response. During deceleration, the motor acts as a generator, feeding power back to the battery state estimation while providing smooth, consistent braking performance.Intelligent Power Assistance ModesThe electric bicycle offers multiple pedal assist settings that match different riding scenarios. The system monitors pedaling intensity and terrain conditions to provide appropriate power support. Over time, the bicycle creates individual power delivery patterns based on each rider's habits. The assist levels range from light support for casual rides to strong assistance for challenging inclines.Built-in Security FeaturesThe bicycle integrates real-time GPS tracking with pinpoint location accuracy. Owners can access remote immobilization controls through their smartphones if theft occurs. The system sends instant alerts for unauthorized movement and tracks the bicycle's position. Additional safety measures include an emergency alert system that notifies preset contacts during accidents or suspicious activities.LED Lighting System with Smart ControlsThe e-bicycle incorporates integrated LED headlights and taillights powered by the main battery system. These lights operate automatically based on ambient light conditions and increase brightness during braking. The lighting system links with the bicycle's central controls, allowing riders to adjust brightness and flash patterns through the handlebar interface. This automated illumination increases rider visibility in low-light conditions and during night rides.Over-the-air Software UpdatesThe Jio e-bicycle receives periodic software improvements through wireless downloads. These updates maintain system performance, add new functions, and fix operational issues. The bicycle's control system manages update installations during idle periods, requiring minimal user input. The process occurs through secure channels, protecting the bicycle's systems from unauthorized access. Users receive notifications before and after successful installations through the Home Assistant companion app.Integration with Jio's Ecosystem of ServicesThe electric bicycle connects with Jio's smart city infrastructure, offering access to digital payment systems, entertainment services, and connected mobility solutions. Users benefit from direct links to JioMart for parts and accessories, JioPay for charging station payments, and JioSaavn for audio during rides. The bicycle's software platform supports future additions to Jio's service portfolio, including potential integration with smart traffic systems and city-wide IoT networks.Comparison with Competitors' Smart FeaturesJio's e-bicycle stands out with its competitive pricing compared to standard electric bikes in the market. While offering a similar range of 50-80 kilometers per charge, Jio Electric Cycle adds value through 5G connectivity and integration with their telecommunications infrastructure. The bicycle matches industry standards for power assistance and battery management but differentiates itself through direct access to Jio's mobile services. This connection to Jio's network provides location tracking and software update capabilities that independent manufacturers cannot match.Expert Opinions on Jio's Smart Bicycle TechnologyBased on the current information available about Jio Electric Cycle technology, industry analysts note that specific expert assessments are limited since the product has not yet reached the market. The absence of real-world testing data and user feedback makes it difficult to evaluate the actual performance of the smart features and their practical benefits. Technical specifications suggest competitive capabilities, but validation of these features will require market introduction and independent testing.User TestimonialsSince Jio's electric bicycle has not yet been released to the market, there are no user experiences or feedback available for analysis. The planned 2025 launch means actual user testimonials, performance reviews, and real-world usage data will become available only after the product reaches consumers. Independent testing and customer feedback will provide insights into the bicycle's practical performance once it enters the market.Potential Drawbacks of the Smart FeaturesThe extensive tracking capabilities of Jio's e-bicycle raise data privacy questions regarding rider location and usage information. The system's reliance on Jio Electric Cycle network coverage might limit full functionality in areas with poor signal strength. Battery-powered smart features could reduce overall range when active, while software updates might interrupt bicycle usage during installation periods. The complex electronics system also increases maintenance costs and repair complexity compared to standard e-bikes.Overall Assessment of the Smart FeaturesJio's electric bicycle combines Intelligent Routing App tracking, power management, and mobile connectivity into an integrated transportation system. The smart features work together to support practical daily commuting while maintaining affordability. The integration with Jio's network infrastructure adds practical benefits through location services and over-the-air updates, though full functionality depends on network access. This combination of technologies makes the bicycle suitable for tech-aware riders seeking connected transportation options.Final Thoughts on Jio's Smart E-BicycleJio's upcoming electric bicycle represents a compelling fusion of accessibility and innovation in the emerging Indian e-mobility sector. While questions remain about privacy concerns and network dependency, the combination of advanced features like GPS tracking, intelligent power management, and seamless mobile integration positions this e-bike as a potential game-changer in urban transportation.The success of this venture will ultimately depend on Jio's ability to deliver on its promises of affordability without compromising on smart functionality. If executed well, this could mark a significant step toward democratizing connected electric mobility in India, setting new standards for what consumers can expect from budget-friendly e-bikes.

blogs.description: Discover the best electric scooters in India for 2025. Compare prices, features, and performance to find affordable, top-rated, and new electric scooters that suit your needs
blogs.content: What is the first thing you see in an electric vehicle? (no… it's not an EV dating site). Best Range? Fastest top speed? Compatibility for a family need? Battery?. Well, is it too much to ask for everything? Every year, the number of options for electric scooters keeps increasing. From this to that, from which to what, the leading companies in the EV segment keep widening their offerings to capture more and more market. While this increase in EVs may or may not cater to the companies, the stocking up of new electric scooters makes audiences confused about what to choose. This year as well, there are many electric scooters launched! So here we are again, with a list of the best electric scooters of 2025 which you can buy according to your needs. To introduce freshness in the shortlisted category, we will be dealing with some new launches in the industry rather than sticking to the previous ones. 5. Honda Activa.eHonda’s foray into the electric scooter market has been highly anticipated, and the Activa.e lives up to the legacy of its petrol-powered predecessors. Combining Honda’s reputation for reliability with electric efficiency, the Activa.e claims to bring a perfect balance of performance and practicality.Key Specs of Activa.e:Battery: Advanced lithium-ion battery with fast-charging capabilityRange: Approx. 150 km on a single chargeTop Speed: 85 km/hDesign: Retains the classic Activa aesthetic with modern electric touchesTechnology: Smart connectivity features including navigation and diagnosticsPrice: ₹1,17,000If you need an electric scooter to cater to the gig economy i.e. for ride-sharing, deliveries etc, this option might give you the comfort and feasibility you have been looking for. Since the electric scooter comes with 2 swappable batteries, it will be a good option for bringing sophistication in rough usage.4. Vida V2 ProThe recently launched Hero MotoCorp’s Vida V2 Pro is another good option in the electric scooter space, offering a combination of powerful performance and smart features.Key Specs of Vida V2 Pro:Battery: 3.9 kWh dual removable batteriesRange: 165 km (IDC certified)Top Speed: 90 km/hAcceleration: 0-40 km/h in 2.9 secondsRiding Modes: Eco, Ride, Sport, CustomDisplay: 7-inch TFT touchscreen with advanced digital controlsRegenerative Braking: Enhances efficiency and extends battery lifeStorage: 26L boot spacePrice: ₹1,15,300One thing is for sure: the Hero Vida is a true fighter in the EV industry, refusing to let any opportunity pass. The scooter is well-suited for young riders who seek quick acceleration and good yet safe speed. It has enough battery for a good range and requires a decent fast charging time—5.5 hours to juice up from 0 to 80%. So, if you need an electric scooter for going to college, then this ride is worth looking into.3. Ampere Magnus NeoAnother on the list is Greaves Electric Mobility Limited’s Ampere Magnus Neo is designed for those seeking affordability without compromising on essential features.Key Specs of Ampere Magnus Neo:Wheels: 12-inch alloy wheels for better stabilityBattery: Advanced LFP (Lithium Iron Phosphate) batteryRange: 100+ km on a single chargeBattery Warranty: 5 years or 75,000 km, whichever comes firstRiding Modes: Three riding modes including a reverse modePortability: Removable and portable battery for convenient chargingPrice: ₹79,999We all have budget restraints. Don’t we? This electric scooter understands the value of money and tries to provide you with all the modern electric scooter facilities a high-tech vehicle provides. The design and features of this electric scooter place it in a family-fit segment. Easy manoeuvrability, manageable weight of 108 kgs and loading capacity of 150 kgs is shouting to get used for daily errands. If you are looking for a family ride, do check this out.2. Bajaj Chetak 3501The Bajaj Chetak 3501 revives the legacy of the iconic Chetak with an electric twist, blending classic design with contemporary electric technology.Key Specs of Chetak 3501:Battery: Robust and durable lithium-ion batteryRange: Approx. 130 km per chargeTop Speed: 95 km/hBuild Quality: Metal body for enhanced durabilitySmart Features: App connectivity for vehicle diagnostics and securityPrice: ₹1,45,000Bajaj Chetak 3501’s build quality and retro-modern design make it a stylish yet practical choice for urban riders.Until now you may be counting features on your fingers, but it's time to put your hands together to welcome Chetak 3501. You might think, the specifications of the electric scooter seem quite average, well it is, but the exceptional service of “Humara Bajaj” and thousands of happy customers have really placed this ride on a very high pedestal. This electric scooter is a green flag for family, office, occasional visits to relatives and daily errands. 1. Ola S1 Pro+ Gen 3The Ola S1 Pro+ Gen 3 redefines the standards for electric scooters with its impressive performance, advanced technology, and futuristic design.Key Specs of Ola S1 Pro+ Gen 3:Battery: 40680 Bharat cells with two options4 kWh battery: 242 km range5 kWh battery: 324 km rangeTop Speed: 128 km/hPower: 13 kW peak power outputSuspension: Premium suspension for a comfortable rideDisplay: Large LCD touchscreen with over-the-air (OTA) software updatesTechnology: Smart connectivity and advanced ride modesPrice: ₹1,54,999Now, here is the boss level. The Ola S1 Pro+ Gen 3 tops our list! Yes, the ride is more expensive than above electric scooters but the wide range of features, power, and performance speaks for itself. This ride is not only suitable for everything we have come across right now, but it adds a new niche of riding– “5th gen”.The electric scooter market in India is thriving, and 2025 brings a wide range of choices for consumers. Whether you prioritize cutting-edge technology, affordability, or a balance of performance and practicality, there’s an electric scooter tailored to your needs. Evaluate your requirements and choose a model that aligns with your lifestyle and budget. With any of these top five models, you’ll be embracing a greener, smarter, and more efficient way of commuting. If you are still confused about any electric vehicle and scratching your head over “what to buy?” then contact us, and we will pave the way for you!

blogs.title: Maruti Suzuki's EV Revolution: How India's Auto Giant Plans to Dominate the Electric Future
blogs.subtitle: In a bold move that could reshape India's automotive landscape, Maruti Suzuki is gearing up to claim 15% of its total sales from electric vehicles ...
blogs.author: Harsh Paliwal
blogs.description: In a bold move that could reshape India's automotive landscape, Maruti Suzuki is gearing up to claim 15% of its total sales from electric vehicles while maintaining its commanding 50% market share.
blogs.content: As India's electric vehicle market surges toward a projected 17 million units by 2030, the country's leading automaker isn't just joining the electric revolution—it's planning to lead it.With an ambitious Rs 7,000 crore investment and plans for six new electric vehicles, Maruti Suzuki is leveraging its massive dealership network and manufacturing expertise to transform from a traditional car manufacturer into an EV powerhouse. The upcoming eVitara marks just the beginning of this electric journey, promising to bring affordable electric mobility to India's growing middle class.Maruti Suzuki's Current EV Market Position and PlansMaruti Suzuki aims to claim 15% of its total sales from electric vehicles while targeting an overall market share of 50% in India. The e VITARA will mark Maruti's first step into the electric segment, supporting their goal of leading green car production and exports in India.Indian EV Market Landscape and Growth ProjectionsIndia's electric vehicle market stands at $8.49 billion in 2024, with projections showing a 40.7% growth rate through 2030. Annual EV sales are expected to hit 17 million units by 2030, with two-wheelers making up nearly half of all electric vehicles sold. Currently, India has 3 million registered EVs, with 56% being two-wheelers.Maruti Suzuki's EV Product Lineup and Development StrategyMaruti Suzuki plans to launch 4 passenger EVs and 2 commercial EVs by 2030, starting with the eVitara. The company will invest Rs 7,000 crore in production facilities, including a new plant in Haryana's Kharkhoda. Their strategy balances small electric SUVs with manufacturing investments and jobs across their range, aiming for increased local manufacturing to keep prices competitive.Partnerships and Collaborations for EV Technology and InfrastructureWhile Maruti Suzuki looks forward to creating a strong presence in India's EV market, details about their technology partnerships remain limited. The company's focus on local manufacturing and upcoming EV launches suggests they will need strong collaborations with partners to support their ambitious goals for 2030.Investment in R&D and Manufacturing Capabilities for EVsMaruti Suzuki aims to allocate Rs 7,000 crore for EV production and research at their new Kharkhoda plant and Suzuki Motor Gujarat facility. The company plans to build total production capacity to 4 million units by 2030. Their manufacturing strategy focuses on increasing local parts production to make EVs more cost-effective for Indian buyers.Pricing and Affordability Strategies for the Indian MarketWhile specific pricing details for Maruti Suzuki's upcoming EVs remain under wraps, the company's focus on local manufacturing points to cost control efforts. The FAME India scheme offers buyers direct purchase incentives, supporting Maruti's market goals. The company's mass-market experience suggests they'll target middle-income buyers with their EV lineup.Addressing Range Anxiety and Charging Infrastructure ChallengesIndia's electric vehicle market has 10,900 public charging stations as of 2022, marking progress in EV infrastructure. Fast-charging options help reduce wait times for drivers, though coverage remains limited. Maruti Suzuki's entry into the EV space comes as charging networks grow across major cities and highways. The company's upcoming e VITARA will need to meet Indian drivers' expectations for range and charging speed to succeed in the market.Leveraging Existing Dealership Network for EV Sales and ServiceWhile specific details about Maruti Suzuki's dealership plans for EVs aren't fully public, the company's strong network puts them in a good position to roll out electric vehicles. As India's largest car maker, Maruti's 3,000+ sales points across the country will need updates to handle EV sales and maintenance. Their sales staff will need new skills to explain electric car features and benefits to first-time EV buyers.Balancing EV Development with Hybrid and ICE Vehicle ProductionMaruti Suzuki aims 15% of sales from electric vehicles and 25% from hybrids by 2030, showing a mixed approach to green transportation. The company will add hybrid technology to affordable models like the Fronx while maintaining its ICE and CNG vehicle lines. This strategy lets Maruti meet different customer needs as the market shifts toward electric mobility.Comparison with Competitors' EV Strategies in IndiaMaruti Suzuki faces stiff competition from Tata Motors, Hyundai, and Mahindra in India's electric car market. While competitors like BYD and Hyundai focus on premium EVs, Maruti's strategy centers on affordable small electric SUVs. The eVitara launch will test the company's ability to match rivals' advanced features while maintaining competitive prices.Government Policies and Incentives Influencing Maruti Suzuki's EV PlansIndia's FAME scheme provides direct benefits for EV buyers, making India's electric vehicle market more attractive to cost-conscious consumers. The government's policy to attract investments in domestic EV manufacturing supports Maruti's local production goals. These incentives help the company's plans to compete in the growing electric vehicle segment while building manufacturing capacity in India.Export Potential for Maruti Suzuki EVsMaruti Suzuki aims to export 7.5-8 lakh vehicles yearly by 2030, using India as a global manufacturing base. Their current infrastructure and planned expansions in Haryana's Kharkhoda and Suzuki Motor Gujarat position them to serve international markets. The company's focus on cost-effective manufacturing and local parts production supports their plans to make India an export hub for electric vehicles.Sustainability Initiatives and Their Impact on EV StrategyOur research notes lack detailed information about Maruti Suzuki's specific sustainability programs tied to their EV plans. The company's shift toward electric vehicles points to environmental priorities, but without concrete data about their green manufacturing practices, carbon reduction goals, or sustainability metrics, we cannot make meaningful claims about their eco-friendly initiatives at this time.Consumer Education and Marketing Approaches for EV AdoptionOur research shows limited information about Maruti Suzuki's specific consumer education and marketing plans for EVs. As India's largest car maker moves into electric vehicles, they will need clear programs to teach buyers about EV benefits, charging needs, and total ownership costs. Their wide dealer network puts them in a strong position to reach potential customers, but details about their marketing strategy remain private.Potential Challenges and Risks in Maruti Suzuki's EV StrategyThe growing competition from Tata Motors, Hyundai, and Tesla's planned entry creates pressure on Maruti's EV plans. Market changes, like the slowdown in European EV sales, signal possible adoption hurdles. The company must also manage production costs while racing to meet their 2030 target of 4 million units. Their focus on India's electric vehicle market requires careful balancing of technology investments with price points that appeal to cost-conscious Indian buyers.Looking Ahead: Maruti Suzuki's Electric FutureAs Maruti Suzuki charts its course toward electric leadership, the company faces both exciting opportunities and significant challenges. Their strategy of balancing affordability with innovation, while leveraging their existing market dominance, positions them uniquely in India's evolving EV landscape.The success of their ambitious plans will depend on their ability to execute on multiple fronts—from manufacturing efficiency to consumer education. Yet, with their deep understanding of the Indian market and substantial investment in EV infrastructure, Maruti Suzuki appears well-equipped to transform India's automotive sector while maintaining their market leadership in the electric era.

blogs.content: OverviewIn India, Electric 3 wheelers are gaining immense popularity among the masses and businesses who want to conserve the environment and promote economical commuting. The Indian Electric auto market in 2025 is robust and expanding which means that you need to be well informed. This document describes what EV 3 wheeler models you should check in India in 2025, the factors one should consider, the model that best suits your needs, the comparison of running and charging expenses, and concludes with a systems overview of the government aid and grants available. Top Factors to Consider When Buying an EV 3-WheelerThere are a number of factors you must focus on and figure out in order to make sure that the electric vehicle meets your business and operational expectations before purchasing an electric 3 wheeler. 1. Battery Energy And Charging: Gauge battery life, distance, and the charging facilities available. Clinch the distance range based on charging points. Further, assess if your daily routes have charging points. Finally, work out if home or work can charge the vehicle.2. Vehicle Range and Performance: Evaluate how far the vehicle can go distances to determine if it meets your travel needs for short commutes or long business deliveries. Also, consider performance aspects like acceleration, top speed, and handling. While Electric 3-wheelers are generally smooth and quiet, the performance does differ between models.3. Cost of Ownership and Incentives: The upfront payment matters, but you should consider long-term costs too - battery replacements, maintenance, and repairs. Maintenance and repair costs for EVs are usually lower than combustion engine vehicles. Investigate if there is any governmental support in the form of subsidies or tax credits that can be used to pay less for the purchase. 4. Cargo Capacity and Design: If the 3-wheeler is going to be used for carrying loads, check the load capacity and design of the vehicle. The specific model should be able to support your load requirements along with any other additional needs. The working conditions are crucial, so the design should include elements of customer satisfaction like how well it protects from the weather as well as the height of the seat. 5. After-Sales Service and Warranty: When choosing a vehicle from a manufacturer, think about the support you would access after buying. Always check if there is a powerful warranty, especially regarding the battery and motor. Another thing to consider is the availability of service centers and spare parts.Top 3-Wheeler Electric Vehicles in India for 2025The following are some of the best electric three wheelers available in India for 2025, based on the needs and constraints of the user. 1. Mahindra Treo Zor: This 3-wheeler is famous for its reliability and performance and is thus widely used in both passenger and cargo transport.2. Euler Motors HiLoad EV: This model is very popular among businesses because of the heavy loading capacity it provides for moving goods.3. Bajaj Maxima XL Cargo E-TEC 12.0: A more expensive low cargo E-3 wheelers, these are also known to have better performance and other premium features.4. Piaggio Ape E Xtra FX: This e-3 wheeler is popular amongst small businesses for its reasonable pricing and better than average efficiency.5. YC Electric E-Loader: It is a good choice for rural and urban areas and is one of the most value-for-money options in the market. It boasts a 1.4kW BLDC motor alongside a range of 75-90 km per charge.6. Greaves Xargo: It is an electric three-wheeler specifically created for small businesses. It has a delivery box and a front tiltable section to enhance turning/loading maneuverability.7. Godawari Eblu Rozee ECO: Added to the list owing to its commendable efficiency, this 3 wheeler is princess transport passenger transport and is powered by a 150Ah Li-ion battery. It can sustain a driving range of 120 km on a single charge.Comparison of Charging & Running Cost:Perhaps the most compelling benefit of electric 3-wheelers is low running costs when compared to CNG. Electric 3-Wheelers cost much more upfront (ranges between INR 3.5 to 4.0 Lakhs) than their ICE counterparts (2.0 to 2.5 Lakhs) but offer value in terms of fuel and maintenance costs.Cost of Running: An electric 3-wheeler costs around INR 50-60 per 100 km, while an ICE 3-wheeler costs around INR 250-300 for the same distance.Savings per Year: If we take an average vehicle travel of 50-80 km daily, at current fuel expenditure, it is possible to save between INR 60,000 to 90,000 per vehicle per year.Electric Vehicle Government Incentives & Subsidies in 2025The government of India has created several incentives and subsidies to promote the usage of electric vehicles (EVs) in the country. Their objective is to reduce the cost barrier and make electric vehicles more affordable to more people.PM E-DRIVE Scheme: This scheme provides subsidies of up to INR 50,000. This amount assists in subsidizing the price difference between electric three-wheelers and ICE models.State Government Incentives: Many states also offer tax holidays and waive registration fees, further decreasing the expenses for EV users.FAME India Scheme: The Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Electric Vehicles (FAME) initiative provision enables the funding of the building of EVs and provides subsidies to enhance their use.

blogs.title: EV charging Infra in 10 years: How does India’s EV future look like
blogs.subtitle: From charging your 1000kW EV in 20-30 mins to EV charging roads, India’s EV infrastructure is paving the way ahead.
blogs.author: Prashant
blogs.description: From charging your 1000kW EV in 20-30 mins to EV charging roads, India’s EV infrastructure is paving the way ahead.
blogs.content: How about we charge your 1000kW EV in 20 to 30 mins? Is it too much? Well, how about we juice up your EV to travel an extra 1000 km in just 10 minutes of charging? And if you don’t want to stop at all, we can charge your vehicle while you are on the way to your destination. Seems like a dream right? Well, the future of electric vehicle charging in India is going to look something like this only. The year 2025 has started with the strong launches and showcase of many electric vehicles, from the everyday Creta EV to the premium-class Porsche Tycan. As companies unveil their high-range electric vehicles, it becomes necessary for the charging infrastructure companies to keep up with the pace. In order to establish a comprehensive EV charging ecosystem, many EV companies are trying to push the charging infra as well. Recently, in one of the biggest contracts ever, Tata.ev has declared to establish 4,00,000 EV charging stations throughout India. The update reflects that the market is moving towards quality as well as quantity. Let’s look at some mind-blowing quality technologies.Solar EV charging SolutionsOne of the biggest USP of electric vehicles is their environmental friendliness and cost-effectiveness. Both factors are usually counter-debated on the argument that the very electricity fueling up the rides is generated via burning coal. However, with India’s push for solar power, these concerns can be resolved in the upcoming years. In fact, the argument still has a very weak ground as India has recorded a 47% share of renewable energy in its total energy consumption, making the electricity you use a bit more greener in shade than you think. Further, it is interesting to note that India has also achieved a historic milestone by surpassing 100 GW of installed solar power capacity, marking a 3450 % increase from the past decade. Although this success is observed throughout various sectors and industries, in the EV market, the most recent application was seen in the Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru, where a brand new solar EV charging station has been established. The charging cost of these solar stations will be significantly lower than that of conventional stations; however, their charging power may also vary. Megawatt Charging Megawatt charging technology has the potential to transform India’s transport and logistics sector by making electric heavy-duty vehicles more practical and efficient. Currently, long charging times limit the viability of electric trucks, buses, and cargo vessels for interstate travel. With megawatt charging, these vehicles can be recharged in minutes instead of hours, keeping them on the road longer and reducing downtime. This will make freight transport faster and more cost-effective, lowering logistics expenses and, in turn, reducing the cost of goods in the market. As India’s economy grows, a reliable and sustainable transport network is essential, and megawatt charging can be a key enabler of this shift.To move in this direction, India has begun investing in advanced charging technology. The launch of a high-tech development facility in Visakhapatnam, in collaboration with Austrian researchers, demonstrates the country’s commitment to building its own high-power charging solutions. Meanwhile, global advancements, such as Comemso’s progress in handling megawatt-scale charging safely and efficiently, highlight the growing feasibility of this technology. By embracing megawatt charging, India can reduce reliance on fossil fuels, lower emissions, and create a cleaner, more efficient transport ecosystem for the future.CATL fast chargingThe CATL’s Shenxing PLUS battery in India, if introduced, could be a game-changer for the country’s electric vehicle (EV) market. With a range exceeding 1,000 kilometres and the ability to add 600 kilometres of charge in just 10 minutes, this technology addresses two of the biggest concerns for Indian EV buyers i.e. range anxiety and long charging times. It goes needless to say, resolving these issues will make long-distance travel seamless, allowing EVs to be practical not just for daily commutes but also for intercity and interstate journeys. Although Shenxing PLUS is not yet available in India, its future entry seems likely as CATL expands its global footprint. If Indian automakers integrate this battery technology, it could make EVs more appealing to a wider audience, especially in regions where long travel distances and limited charging stations are concerns. Additionally, if CATL’s superfast charging network model is implemented in India, it could complement the country’s growing charging infrastructure, further accelerating the shift toward electric mobility. With the right industry partnerships, Shenxing PLUS could help India achieve its clean energy goals faster while making EVs more practical, efficient, and accessible for millions. Although the company’s tech is an augmented technology in existing Indian OEMs like Revolt, its complete potential is yet not unlocked. However, China already controls a significant share of the global battery supply chain, and wider adoption of CATL’s technology in India could slow down domestic innovation and manufacturing capabilities. India has been pushing for battery indigenization through initiatives like the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme to promote local battery manufacturing. While integrating CATL’s advanced technology could benefit the Indian market in the short term, over-reliance on Chinese imports might limit the growth of homegrown alternatives.Dash Dynamics The concept of electric vehicle (EV) charging roads, where vehicles can wirelessly charge as they drive, is gaining global attention as a transformative solution for sustainable transportation. Norway recently inaugurated the world's first wireless charging road in Trondheim, enabling electric buses to operate continuously without stopping for charging, thereby reducing carbon emissions. This pilot project utilizes specialized copper coils embedded beneath the road surface, allowing vehicles equipped with compatible technology to change dynamically. In India, the adoption of such innovative infrastructure could significantly enhance the EV ecosystem. By integrating wireless charging into major highways and urban roads, EVs could maintain optimal battery levels without the need for frequent stops, addressing range anxiety—a common barrier to EV adoption. This would make long-distance travel more feasible for electric vehicles, promoting wider acceptance among consumers and contributing to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions.Although this application seems like a distant future, believe me, it’s not that far! Indian companies are actively exploring this technology. Dash Dynamic, for instance, has developed a wireless charging solution that charges EVs 30% faster than conventional plug-in chargers. Their system employs magnetic resonance-based technology, enabling efficient energy transfer without physical connectors. Such advancements indicate a promising future for wireless charging infrastructure in India. However, this dynamic EV charging road is the greater application of the company’s current offering. As of now, the company features a wireless charging setup with 2 step installation. At first, the electric vehicle will be equipped with a receiver and power converter, after which the vehicle has to be parked upon the transmitter pad connected to a wall unit. This setup will allow your vehicle to get charged wirelessly. Implementing EV charging roads in India would require substantial investment and collaboration between government agencies, private enterprises, and technology providers. Challenges such as infrastructure costs, technological standardization, and vehicle compatibility need to be addressed. However, the potential benefits—including seamless charging experiences, extended driving ranges, and decreased reliance on extensive charging station networks—make it a compelling avenue for India's sustainable transportation strategy.As global examples like Norway's wireless charging road demonstrate the feasibility and advantages of this technology, India has the opportunity to leapfrog into the next generation of EV infrastructure. By embracing wireless charging roads, the country can accelerate its transition to electric mobility, reduce environmental impact, and enhance energy efficiency in the transportation sector.Pretty interesting HUH? If these futuristic ideas have convinced you about the future of mobility, then contact EVINDIA to own an electric ride. And be a part of today’s future!

blogs.title: Ola S1 Pro+ Gen 3: Pushing the Boundaries of Electric Scooters
blogs.subtitle: Discover the Ola S1 Pro+ Gen 3, featuring the cutting-edge 40680 Bharat cell, up to 324 km range, 128 km/h top speed & smart connectivity. Explore ...
blogs.author: Akshesh
blogs.description: Discover the Ola S1 Pro+ Gen 3, featuring the cutting-edge 40680 Bharat cell, up to 324 km range, 128 km/h top speed & smart connectivity. Explore Ola’s Gen 3 lineup now!
blogs.content: Ola Electric once again sets a new benchmark in the two-wheeler electric industry with its launching of the new S1 Pro+ Gen 3. Its headline feature will be the 40680 Bharat cell, which will come with an excellent range of up to 324 km per charge, the highest in the e-scooter segment. Ola has successfully been able to bring out a product for every segment in its Gen 3 lineup, from daily commuters, and gig workers, to luxury riders. The latest launches will further affirm Ola's commitment to sustainability, innovation, and efficiency in the Indian EV market.Bhavish Aggarwal, chairman and managing director of Ola Electric, said, “With our first generation of scooters, we offered customers a truly aspirational electric scooter that kickstarted the EV revolution in the country. With Gen 2, we made our scooters smarter and more accessible by expanding our portfolio with scooters for every Indian across every price range,” a press release by the company reported.He further said, “Today, with Gen 3, we are taking the EV two-wheeler industry to the ‘next level’. Gen 3 is bringing unmatched performance, superior efficiency, and reinventing benchmarks we set for ourselves, which will change the industry all over again,” the release added.The Ola Gen 3 LineupOla Gen 3 is the new product lineup of four main models of Ola for different customer requirements, with two battery variants each.Ola S1X Gen 3The Ola S1X Gen 3 is perfect for urban commuters seeking affordability and smart features. It offers three battery options: The 2 kWh battery ride has a range of 108 km, a top speed of 101 km/hr, and a quick acceleration of 0-40 km/hr in just 3.4 seconds. The Ola S1X 3 kWh Gen 3 variant features 176 km of range, a top speed of 115 km/hr, and acceleration from 0-40 km/hr in just 3.1 seconds.The highest trim level– the 4 kWh dual battery variant provides up to 242 km per charge. The motor of 5.5 kW, a top speed of 123 km/h and a 7-inch touchscreen display for navigation and connectivity, makes the ride a thrilling yet practicable option.Ola S1X+ Gen 3Another option for those seeking a balance between performance and affordability is the Ola S1X+. It offers a 4 kWh battery with a range of 242 km and a peak power of 11kW. The vehicle can accelerate from 0-40 km in just 3 seconds. With Enhanced seat ergonomics, A full chain cover, and a 4.3-inch colour segmented display, the vehicle is a whole package of performance and style you can ask for. Ola S1 Pro Gen 3The Ola S1 Pro Gen 3 is an electric scooter with a high-end look for those in search of premium performance. The standard battery capacity is 3 kWh with a range of 176 km and a top speed of 117 km/hr, and the extended battery goes up to 4 kWh with a range of 242 km. It boasts a top speed of 125 km/h with a peak power of 11kW and includes advanced features like cruise control, multiple riding modes, and enhanced smart connectivity. Ola S1 Pro+ Gen 3The Ola S1 Pro+ is the flagship model in the series, which uses the latest 40680 Bharat cell technology. It comes with two options of batteries: a standard 4 kWh battery with an IDC range of 242 km. The vehicle comes with a peak power of 13kW and a top speed of 128 km/h. It also comes with premium suspension, a large LCD touchscreen, and OTA software updates. Another variant of the vehicle comes equipped with a 5kWh variant which powers up the ride to travel a whopping distance of 320 kms on a single charge and an exhilarating top speed of 128 km/hr.Other Offerings from OlaApart from its Gen 3 lineup, the company has furthered its portfolio with more models for particular segments. The Ola S1Z was scheduled to be launched in May 2025 as a lightweight commuter scooter. In terms of specifications, it has removable dual 1.5 kWh batteries and is said to offer a range of up to 146 km along with a top speed of 70 km/h. It packs an LCD display and a physical key start. The product is priced at Rs 59,999. The Ola S1Z+, which will also be launched in May 2025, has the same specs but is designed for dual-purpose usage and is priced at Rs 64,999.For gig workers, Ola has introduced the Ola Gig and Ola Gig+, both launching in April 2025. The Ola Gig is designed for short-distance deliveries, featuring a 1.5 kWh removable battery, 112 km range, and 25 km/h top speed, priced at Rs 39,999. The Ola Gig+ is designed for more extended travel distances and more payload, which includes single or dual battery types with an 81 km range with a single battery 157 km with two batteries and a 45 km/h top speed.Ola also hinted that they will soon introduce an electric roadster bike series, aimed at bringing high-performance electric motorcycles to the Indian market. As of now, all details remain unrevealed; however, it indicates the further expansion of Ola in the premium electric two-wheeler segment.Ola and InnovationOla is working towards creating a holistic ecosystem for electric mobility. The innovations that the company has been bringing to the table, such as the Ola Power Pod, are a testament to its efforts in improving charging infrastructure and battery technology. Smart features are also an important aspect of today's tech-driven world, and that is why the MOVE OS 5 update comes with AI-powered smart connectivity, an LCD dashboard, and over-the-air (OTA) software updates. These advancements ensure that Ola riders stay ahead in technology, efficiency, and traffic management.Wondering where to buy this tech revolution? Call us at +91 9099900348 and book your ride now.

blogs.title: Top 10 e-Bikes in India: Best Speed, Range, and Features
blogs.subtitle: Discover the top 10 e-bikes in India with the best speed, range, and features. Compare electric bikes for performance, style, and value to find you...
blogs.author: Prashant
blogs.description: Discover the top 10 e-bikes in India with the best speed, range, and features. Compare electric bikes for performance, style, and value to find your perfect ride!
blogs.content: The thrill of twisting the throttle and letting go of your bike against the wind blanket is surely euphoric. The cold nose afterwards as a souvenir of your journey is embraced by everyone, I believe. Well, good for you, these thrilling rides are now available in the electric version as well. Why electric? Because the very breeze freshly and abruptly hitting your face needs to be taken care of. Isn’t it? The Indian electric bike market has decided to take care of your precious rides and the extra precious environment as well. With a range of electric bike models, users now have the option to enjoy cutting-edge technology and superior performance instead of conventional smoke-throwing bikes. If you're also looking for the best electric bike in India, here’s a list of the top 10 e-bikes in India based on their speed, range, and features.10. PureEV EcodryftA commuter-friendly electric bike, PureEV Ecodryft is designed for efficiency and comfort. With a top speed of 75 km/h and a range between 131 km and 171 km, it is designed for family needs such as running errands and office-going. The 3.5 kWh portable battery adds convenience, while features like Reverse Mode, Hill-Start Assist, Down-Hill Assist, Parking Assist, Smart AI for Battery Longevity, and Regenerative Braking make this bike stand out in its segment. The top variant of the bike i.e. the Pure EV Ecodryft 350 costs ₹ 1,09,999. 9. Pure EV eTryst XAnother bike in the Pure EV fleet, the eTryst X is also worth looking. The eTryst X offers a city ride with a top speed of 85 km/h and a range of 111-171 km. This bike also comes with a 3.5 kWh battery and ensures sustained performance in your intra and inter-city commutes. Meanwhile, advanced features such as Smart AI for Battery Longevity, Parking Assist, Coasting Regen, and a Highly Efficient Powertrain make it a great option for urban riders looking for reliability and power. The Pure EV eTryst X will cost you around ₹1,49,999 (ex-showroom).8. Ferrato DisruptorIf you love bulky fangs on your bike, this might be the right ride for you. The Ferrato Disruptor is a high-performance e-bike with a top speed of 95 km/h, thanks to its 3.97 kWh battery. The vehicle boasts 45 Nm nominal torque and 228 Nm peak torque, ensuring rapid acceleration and superior handling. The bike has a range of 109 km per charge and an impressive cost-effectiveness of 25 paise per kilometre, making it an exciting choice. The heavy-looking Ferrato Disruptor will cost your ₹1,60,051(ex-showroom).7. Odyssey EvoqisWant some more power in the same look? Odyssey got you covered. If power is what you seek, the Odyssey Evoqis delivers with a 3000W motor and a peak power of 4300W. With a maximum speed of 80 km/h and a range of 140 km, it ensures seamless rides. The front and rear disc brakes enhance safety, while the stylish design makes it a head-turner on the roads. The Odyssey Evoqis will charge your pocket Rs. 1,71,250 (ex-showroom). 6. Revolt RV1+The Revolt RV1+ is a practical and efficient e-bike with a top speed of 70 km/h and an impressive range of 160 km. Its 3.24 kWh battery supports fast charging (0-80% in just 1 hour 20 minutes). The twin shocker rear suspension and telescopic forks provide a comfortable ride, making it a great choice for city commutes. The Revolt RV1+ is designed as a multi-utility family ride which can be driven around by drivers of any age. The Revolt RV1+ will cost you ₹99,990.5. MATTER AERA 5000+This stylish street-fighter-inspired bike is equipped with a 10kW motor and a 5kWh fixed battery, offering a 125 km range. It comes with a four-speed gearbox, making it one of the few e-bikes with gears. Three riding modes (Eco, City, and Sport), smartphone connectivity, keyless operation, and a digital instrument console make the MATTER AERA 5000+ a futuristic option.The ride itself is a statement of design and fashion which is appealing mostly to youth riders. The MATTER AERA 5000+Will cost you ₹ 1,73,999 (ex-showroom).4. Oben Rorr EZ (4.4 kWh)A dynamic choice for riders seeking power and efficiency, the Oben Rorr EZ boasts a top speed of 95 km/h and an exceptional range of 579 km. Its MHX best-in-class heat management system, 277 Nm torque, IP67 waterproof battery, and remote diagnostics enhance its appeal. Additionally, it charges in just 2 hours and features geo-fencing theft protection.3. Ola Roadster XAre these bikes going out of your budget? Well check this bike out. Ola’s Roadster X offers three battery options: 2.5 kWh, 3.5 kWh, and 4.5 kWh. The top variant provides a 200 km range, accelerates 0-60 km/h in just 2.8 seconds, and reaches a top speed of 124 km/h. The bike includes Advanced Regen, Cruise Control, Reverse Mode, Geo and Time Fencing, Theft Detection, and Tyre Pressure Alerts, making it one of the smartest e-bikes in the market. One of the most amazing things about this bike which makes it further worthy of getting included in the top 10 electric bikes of India is its price. The Ola Roadster X starting price is just ₹74,999 (ex-showroom).2. Ola Roadster ProSimilar to its sibling, the Ola Roadster is built for performance, offering a top speed of 194 km/h and a maximum range of 579 km. The vehicle will be in two variants 8kWh and 16kWh. The vehicle will feature Krutrim Voice Assistant, Smart Park, Group Navigation, Cruise Control, DIY Mode, and Emergency SOS Alert, setting a new benchmark in electric mobility. The Ola Roadster Pro (16kWh) will cost around ₹ 2,49,999.1. Ultraviolette F99Well, drum rolls please! Taking the top spot is the Ultraviolette F99, an electric sports bike engineered for sheer performance. With an astounding top speed of 265 km/h, it is one of the fastest electric motorcycles in India. The bike produces 200 Nm of torque, ensuring lightning-fast acceleration and exhilarating rides. Weighing 180 kg, the F99 is aerodynamically designed to maximize speed and efficiency. Its 10 kWh battery system ensures optimal performance for high-speed touring. You will be surprised to know that Ultraviolette F99 has become the fastest Indian-manufactured motorcycle ever (take that ICE bikes). Yes, the vehicle was able to achieve a 258kmph in just 10.712 seconds. The price of this bike is a bit more than any usual electric bike you see in the Indian Market. However, if you are only concerned with higher performance and can go at the higher-end rates then this bike is for you. The Ultraviolette F99 will cost you ₹8 Lakhs (ex-showroom).Final Thoughts? Our top 10 electric bikes in India have made one thing evident: the Indian e-bike market is expanding rapidly, offering consumers a variety of choices tailored to different needs. Whether you are looking for a budget-friendly city commuter or a high-speed performance beast, there is an electric two-wheeler for you. With advancements in battery technology, smart features, and safety enhancements, these e-bikes are not just eco-friendly alternatives but also futuristic machines that redefine commuting in India.

blogs.title: BYD Sealion 7: “Making waves” at the Bharat Mobility Expo 2025
blogs.subtitle: Experience the BYD Sealion 7, a luxury electric SUV debuting at Bharat Mobility Expo 2025. With sleek design, advanced features, and a long-range b...
blogs.author: Prashant
blogs.description: Experience the BYD Sealion 7, a luxury electric SUV debuting at Bharat Mobility Expo 2025. With sleek design, advanced features, and a long-range blade battery, it’s set to redefine India’s EV market.
blogs.content: BYD (Build Your Dreams), the global leader in new energy vehicles (NEVs), is all set to captivate the Indian market with its futuristic electric SUV, the BYD Sealion 7, which will be showcased at the upcoming Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025. Known for its rivalry with Tesla, BYD with its new offering may tap the luxury market of the Indian EV industry. The company’s innovative technologies and sustainability-driven vision will be reflected in its latest offering. The entry of the Sealion 7 will mark another significant step in revolutionising the electric vehicle (EV) landscape.What Makes the BYD Sealion 7 Unique?A Design Inspired by the SeaThe Sealion 7 features an exclusive ocean-inspired design, an Idea manifested in life by BYD's Global Design Director, Wolfgang Egger. The SUV's aesthetic is a nod to the fluidity and power of ocean waves, featuring a sleek, aerodynamic silhouette with the signature 'Ocean X' front styling. This design philosophy is not just skin deep; it's integrated into the vehicle's performance through technologies like Intelligent Torque Active Control (iTAC) and Cell-to-body (CTB). The latter integrates the battery directly into the vehicle's structure, enhancing space efficiency and vehicle stability.Bold and Aerodynamic DesignInspired by the ocean, the Sealion 7 has a sleek, futuristic aesthetic crafted by Wolfgang Egger, BYD’s Global Design Director. With its dynamic curves and aerodynamic structure, the SUV is not only visually appealing but also highly efficient. It is designed similarly to the Seal's LED headlights. The Sealion 7 features air curtains on the bumpers to improve the electric SUV's aerodynamics even further. The car will most likely have a sloping roofline and flush door handles on the side, giving it a coupe appearance. With a motorised tailgate, it features a connected LED DRL and taillamp at the back.Advanced Performance CapabilitiesThe Sealion 7 is equipped with BYD’s Intelligent Torque Active Control (iTAC) system and the Cell-to-Body (CTB) technology. These features provide outstanding stability, safety, and road performance, making it a standout in the mid-size electric SUV segment.Exceptional Battery RangeThe vehicle features an AWD powertrain, Moreover, powered by a blade battery, the vehicle can reach 0-100 km/h in just 4.5 seconds. In the global market, the vehicle comes in three battery packs. However, it is yet to be known which variant of the vehicle will be launched in India. However, Market analysts are suggesting that it might appear in two battery options—82.5 kWh and 91.3 kW which will power the Sealion 7 to deliver an expected driving range of up to 502 kilometres on a single charge, ensuring a worry-free long-distance driving experience. Judging from the globally available Sealipon-7, the vehicle may come with the following luxury features–Interior and Features (expected)The Sealion 7 may come packed with modern amenities, including:1-A 15.6-inch rotating touchscreen for infotainment.2-Nappa leather seats for enhanced comfort.3-128-color ambient lighting for a premium in-car atmosphere.4-A 12-speaker Dynaudio system that provides an immersive audio experience.BYD’s Journey in IndiaBYD has been operational in India for over 17 years and is steadily expanding its footprint in the market. The company plans to increase its dealership network from 27 to 40 outlets by the end of 2025, reflecting its commitment to the Indian EV market. However, the company’s Chinese origin impedes its expansion in India. In 2023, the government of India, citing security concerns declined to let BYD set up a $1bn worth factory in India. With the company’s new launch, it will be interesting to note the consumer behaviour of Indians.The Sealion 7 is expected to strengthen BYD’s position in India alongside its existing models such as the BYD Atto 3 and BYD E6. With the electric four-wheeler market expected to grow up to 10% in 2025, BYD’s advanced EV offerings are well-timed to meet the demand for reliable and efficient electric vehicles.Market Impact and CompetitionScheduled for launch in India by the first quarter of 2025, the Sealion 7 is poised to make a significant impact. With an expected price tag starting around Rs 45 lakh to Rs 55 lakh (ex-showroom), it enters the fray alongside competitors like the Kia EV6 and Hyundai IoniqHowever, its blend of performance, design, and technology might set it apart, appealing to those who seek luxury brands.A Step Forward for India’s EV RevolutionThe launch of the BYD Sealion 7 in India is an exciting development for EV enthusiasts and sustainability advocates. With its advanced features, long-range blade battery, and ocean-focused luxury design, the Sealion 7 will be a competent product in the Indian EV market.As BYD continues to expand its presence and introduce groundbreaking technologies, the Sealion 7’s debut is a clear indication of the company’s ambition to further spread its legs in the EV industry amid India’s effort to transition towards electric mobility.Stay tuned for more updates from BYD at the Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025 where the Sealion 7 and other innovative models will take center stage.

blogs.title: VinFast EV’s India Debut: A Reciprocative Trust Between Tech and Market
blogs.subtitle: After opening a facility in Tamil Nadu, VinFast gears up to launch VF7 and VF9 at Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025
blogs.author: Prashant
blogs.description: After opening a facility in Tamil Nadu, VinFast gears up to launch VF7 and VF9 at Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025
blogs.content: Well, it can be said that we can see the upcoming Bharat Mobility Global Expo as a conjecture of private and public efforts done in the last few years to transition the market from ICE to electric vehicles. The potential of the Indian market is well reflected in the fact that the Vietnamese company VinFast has chosen India as its fourth global EV market after Canada, the USA and Europe. The consumer-driven market of India needs affordable high-tech rides that can serve well on Indian roads and varying terrains. Amidst the attempt to provide such transformation, VinFast has emerged as a promising player, bringing its innovative EV solutions to market in India and across the globe. Now, with its first foray into India through Bharat Mobility, VinFast is ready to disrupt the Indian EV market with its promise of technological superiority and sustainable mobility.Who is VinFast?VinFast, a subsidiary of the Vietnamese conglomerate Vingroup, is relatively new to the automotive industry, having been founded in 2017. Despite its young age, VinFast has quickly made a name for itself with its ambitious vision and rapid product development. The brand debuted in the global automotive arena with internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles but swiftly transitioned to focus exclusively on EVs by 2021. This bold pivot underscores its commitment to driving the world toward a greener future.With a strong emphasis on cutting-edge technology, sustainability, and customer-centric designs, VinFast has established a presence in several international markets, including the United States, Europe, and now India. Its entry into the Indian market through Bharat Mobility is a strategic move that reflects the growing potential of India as a key player in the global EV ecosystem.Why India? The Potential of the Indian EV MarketIndia is one of the world's fastest-growing automotive markets, with a population exceeding 1.4 billion and increasing urbanisation. However, the penetration of EVs in the Indian automotive market is still relatively low, accounting for less than 2% of total vehicle sales as of 2024. The researchers have indicated that this number is going to rise significantly in the year 2025, with the four-wheeler EV market expected to see a penetration of about 10%. This gap is filled by the EV manufacturers who are all set to introduce innovative products tailored to Indian consumers' needs.Several factors make India a promising market for EVs:Government Initiatives: Policies like the Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles (FAME) scheme, subsidies, and incentives on EV purchases encourage consumers to switch to electric mobility.Environmental Awareness: With rising air pollution levels in major cities, the demand for cleaner, greener alternatives is on the rise.Growing Infrastructure: The expansion of EV charging networks and renewable energy sources makes it more feasible for consumers to adopt EVs. According to a report by Forvis Mazars, “With the number of public charging stations increasing from 1,800 in early 2022 to over 16,000 by March 2024, the landscape is evolving rapidly.”Cost Sensitivity: Indian consumers are highly cost-conscious, and the promise of lower running costs for EVs compared to traditional ICE vehicles is a significant draw.Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme: India's PLI scheme has been successful in attracting global manufacturers to set up operations in the country. The fact that VinFast opened a manufacturing plant in Tamil Nadu six months ahead of schedule in the first half of 2025 speaks to the effectiveness of the scheme. The facility is in line with India's 'Make in India' initiative but also speaks to the commitment of VinFast to localizing production to reduce costs and create more jobs.As such, this is going to be one of the major production facilities for VinFast Electric Vehicles in India. As such, it will provide more localized solutions for the market while supporting the government's goals of electrification and self-reliance in the automobile sector.Showcasing Innovation at Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025VinFast is set to make waves at the upcoming Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025, scheduled from January 17 to 21. Among the highlights are two of its most anticipated electric sports utility vehicles (SUVs): the VF 7 and VF 9.The VF 7: Sleek Design Meets PerformanceThe VF7 electric car is a five-seater sporty ride which comes with a swoopy, crossover-like appearance complemented by sleek lights at the front and rear in a design of VinFast’s “V”, symbolising innovation and vision. In markets outside of its home country, the VF 7 is supplied in two variations: Eco, with a net 75.3kWh battery pack and, another with a similar net 75.3kWh battery pack.Performance: The Eco variant features a single motor delivering 204 horsepower and 310 Nm of torque, while the Plus variant boasts a dual-motor setup, offering 354 horsepower and 500 Nm of torque.Range: The Eco trim has a WLTP-rated range of 450 km, and the Plus variant offers 431 km.Technology: Both trims come equipped with a Level 2 Advanced Driver Assistance System (ADAS) suite. The Eco trim features a 12.9-inch infotainment touchscreen, while the Plus variant is upgraded to a 15-inch screen.Wheels: Alloy wheels vary by trim, with 19 inches for the Eco and 20 or 21 inches for the Plus.The VF 7 is a testament to VinFast’s ability to blend aesthetics, functionality, and advanced technology, making it an ideal choice for Indian urban and semi-urban consumers.The VF 9: Redefining Luxury and UtilityAs the largest e-SUV in VinFast’s lineup, the VF 9 is designed for families and adventure enthusiasts. This three-row SUV can comfortably seat six or seven passengers and boasts dimensions larger than the Audi Q7.Performance: Both the Eco and the Plus variants will have a 123kWh battery pack with a dual-motor all-wheel drive, with 408 horsepower and 620 Nm of torque. The Eco can accelerate from 0-40 km/h in 6.6 seconds, while the Plus does it in 6.7 seconds, depending on the seating configuration.Range: The VF 9 offers an impressive WLTP-rated range of up to 531 km, ensuring the solution to your range anxiety.Luxury Features: From spacious interiors to advanced infotainment systems, the VF 9 caters to consumers seeking both luxury and practicality.These models highlight VinFast’s commitment to catering to diverse customer needs, from urban professionals to large families.What Sets VinFast Apart?VinFast’s entry into the Indian market is a testament to its confidence in delivering value and innovation. But what truly sets the brand apart from its competitors?1. Technological SuperiorityVinFast has consistently invested in state-of-the-art technology to ensure its EVs offer an unparalleled driving experience. The VF comes with an AWD powertrain and two motors delivering 402 HP making the ride stand out in performance terms. Features like smart parking assist can assist the driver in entering and exiting parking spaces by navigating from parallel, perpendicular, or inclined parking locations. The vehicle also comes with Blind Spot detection which supports a safe lane change manoeuvre by using radar sensors to alert drivers of the objects in the blind spots. Moreover, advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), over-the-air (OTA) updates, and integrated AI-based solutions add feather in the cap.﻿2. Sustainability FocusFrom adopting renewable energy in manufacturing facilities to focusing on eco-friendly materials in vehicle interiors, VinFast emphasizes reducing its carbon footprint. Its commitment to battery recycling and second-life applications contributes to a circular economy.3. Customer-Centric ApproachVinFast ensures its vehicles are adaptable to diverse market conditions, designing for durability and cost-efficiency tailored to Indian roads and consumer preferences.4- Aesthetics like never beforeThe vehicle comes with “Premium Innovation With 3 Rows of Seating For 7 People,” making the ride suitable for your large family. The configuration gives the ride a bulky look. VinFast has featured an on-of-its-kind Glass Roof in its ride. The interior of the vehicle is also designed very sophisticatedly, as seen in the ride’s dynamic ambient lighting that can be customized according to your mood. Vegan leather hugs the seats of the vehicle and the digital cockpit makes the ride an aesthetical statement. 5- Safety reimaginedWhile manufacturing the VF series it seems like the company has paid a special emphasis on the user’s safety. In the vehicle, ADAS helps keep you and your passenger safe with features including collision warning, fully automatic parking assist, remote parking, on-ramp and off-ramp assistance, cruise assistance, motorway driving aid, auto lane-changing assist, and summon mode. A Bright Future: Transforming Indian MobilityVinFast’s partnership with Bharat Mobility, coupled with its showcase at the Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025, underscores its ambition to lead India’s EV revolution. With cutting-edge technology, sustainable practices, and customer-centric designs, VinFast is set to redefine mobility in India.As India accelerates toward a greener future, collaborations like this will shape the narrative of sustainable transportation for generations to come. VinFast and Bharat Mobility are poised to lead this transformation, one innovative EV at a time.

blogs.title: NDS Eco Motors: Pioneering Affordable, High-Range Electric Mobility at Bharat Mobility Expo 2025

blogs.author: Prashant
blogs.description: Discover NDS Eco Motors' groundbreaking electric scooters with up to 218km range, redefining sustainable and affordable mobility at Bharat Mobility Expo 2025. Perfect for urban commutes and last-mile deliveries.
blogs.content: Rage anxiety is one of the biggest impediments to EV adoption. Companies in the EV industry are continuously working to solve this issue by developing electric vehicles that can travel longer on a single charge and do not need frequent charging. You will be amazed to know that NDS Eco Motors has achieved to develop a range of electric scooters that can go up to a whopping 218kms on a single charge. Yes, you read it right!Ranging from delivery-centric electric scooters to everyday inter or intra-city commutes the NDS Eco Motors emerges as a beacon of practicality and inclusivity. Since its humble beginnings in 2015, this Bangalore-based innovator has been redefining what electric mobility means for the everyday Indian. With models like the SQD and E2C, the company is dedicated to offering a vision of sustainable transport that's both accessible and effective. As the Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025 approaches, NDS stands ready to showcase how they've bridged the gap between high-end electric vehicles and the needs of the mass market.The Journey of NDS Eco Motors: From Vision to ImpactNDS Eco Motors set out with a mission to democratize electric mobility. With an authorized share capital of Rs. 95,000,000 and a paid-up capital of Rs. 55,000,000, they've claimed to develop an electric vehicle which comes with affordability without compromising on utility. NDS Eco Motors first entered the market with its ARAI-approved model, ALFA, followed by the launch of the advanced LIO and LIO+ variants, featuring cutting-edge lithium-ion batteries. These models meet ARAI homologation standards and qualify for FAME I incentives, highlighting the company’s commitment to quality and sustainability in electric mobility.In total, the company offers 2 electric scooters SQD and E2C in different variants. The SQD electric scooter variants come with the following specifications–Both the SQD and E2C offerings of the company come in five variants including Pro, Pro Max, Pro Max+, Ultra+, and Ultra Max. All vehicles come equipped with BLDC Motors and a fixed battery. Ensuring safety, the SQD and E2C electric scooters feature disc brakes, twin telescopic suspension at the front and drum brake, and twin shock absorbers at the rear. Through their 'Make in India' ethos, NDS has tailored their scooters for the diverse Indian terrains, achieving sales from hundreds to thousands post-launch, proving there's a market hungry for practical electric solutions.Leading Edge in Eco-Friendly Scooter InnovationThe Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2025 is the perfect stage for NDS Eco Motors to shine. Here, they plan to unveil their latest innovations, including the company’s delivery-centric electric scooter–E2C-D which also claims a range of 218km in its Pro Max + variant. The other variants of the scooter are E2C-D Pro and E2C-D Pro Max. As per the company, the E2C-D is India’s 1st ARAI-approved electric two-wheeler scooter designed to cater to the growing demand for eco-friendly last-mile delivery solutions. The vehicle can revolutionize the delivery segment of e-commerce as we understand and may come out as a cost-saving alternative. Attendees will witness NDS's commitment to expanding their product line, with a focus on integrating even more advanced battery technology to go beyond the current range. It's not just about showcasing products; it's about demonstrating how NDS envisions a future where electric mobility is not only a luxury but a norm, both in India and potentially on the global stage.Innovation and Sustainability: The NDS WayAt the heart of NDS's narrative is innovation tailored for the Indian context. Their innovation centre has been the crucible for developing scooters that not only fit the budget but also excel in performance. Features like regenerative braking are not just buzzwords here; they're practical solutions that extend range and promote sustainability. NDS has mastered the art of making lithium-ion batteries work within India's variable climate, ensuring their scooters are as reliable in the sweltering heat of Chennai as they are in the cooler climes of Shimla.  Their proactive approach extends to after-sales support, with a growing network of dealers and service centres across urban India, fostering trust in electric mobility by addressing one of its biggest challenges: maintenance.The company’s E2C variant is another example of the company’s technological superiority. The multipurpose vehicle offers the following–NDS Eco Motors: Shaping the Future of Urban TransportAs we look to the future, NDS Eco Motors isn't merely expanding its product catalogue; they're reimagining urban transport. The Bharat Mobility Expo will serve as a glimpse into their plans for smart mobility integration, where NDS scooters could play a pivotal role in smart city developments, aiding in traffic management and energy efficiency. There's also a whisper of potential partnerships with renewable energy providers for solar-powered charging solutions, pushing the envelope on reducing the carbon footprint of personal transport.
